findings.failure_scenario: A user runs the block with model "Flux Kontext Pro": the stored node input `model` is the enum value "Flux Kontext Pro" (the frontend can only send the JSON-schema enum values), but `_is_cost_filter_match` (backend/executor/utils.py:158) compares it against "black-forest-labs/flux-kontext-pro" from the filter, which is never equal. Neither the 10-credit nor 20-credit BlockCost matches, `_charge_usage` never calls spend_credits, and every run of this paid Replicate block is free. The existing LLM_COST convention filters on the enum member itself (block_cost_config.py:104-132), which str-enums compare equal to their value — the filter here should use FluxKontextModelName.PRO/MAX instead of .api_name.
findings.summary: Cost filters keyed on FluxKontextModelName.api_name ("black-forest-labs/flux-kontext-pro"/"-max") can never match the runtime input value, so block_usage_cost returns 0 and users are never charged for this block

findings.failure_scenario: A graph chains a media-producing block into input_image — e.g. FileStoreBlock, whose documented output is "The relative path to the stored file in the temporary directory" (backend/blocks/basic.py:20) — giving a value like "exec_file/<exec_id>/cat.png". run_model sends input_params["input_image"] = "exec_file/<exec_id>/cat.png" to Replicate's flux-kontext endpoint, which requires "a URL or base64-encoded data URI" for input_image, so the prediction fails with a 422/invalid-input error. The block should convert via store_media_file(..., return_content=True) (backend/util/file.py) like other blocks that hand media to external APIs.
findings.summary: input_image is passed to the Replicate API without conversion, so local relative-path media values (a first-class MediaFileType per backend/util/type.py:220) are sent to Replicate, which can only fetch URLs or data URIs

findings.failure_scenario: The block's test fixture registers its credentials meta input with title "api_key" instead of "Mock Replicate API key". Any consumer that displays or resolves the test-input credentials by title (e.g. the block test-run UI or future test-store lookups keyed on CredentialsMetaInput.title, backend/data/model.py:286) shows/writes the wrong credential name; compare the correct "title": TEST_CREDENTIALS.title in backend/blocks/ai_image_generator_block.py:324.
findings.summary: TEST_CREDENTIALS_INPUT copies the wrong field: "title" is set to TEST_CREDENTIALS.type ("api_key") instead of TEST_CREDENTIALS.title ("Mock Replicate API key")

findings.failure_scenario: A user following the docs wires the next node to the "image_url" output of this block; the platform offers only "output_image" (and "error"), so the documented connection cannot be made and the user's graph silently lacks the edited-image result.
findings.summary: Documentation lists the output as "image_url", but the block's Output schema and run() yield "output_image" (flux_kontext.py:94,141), so the doc teaches a non-existent output key

findings.failure_scenario: The three copies already drift (this one raises ValueError("No output received") where the siblings return a fallback string, and only this copy lacks the "list item is a string" branch comment handling): any future change to replicate SDK output handling or the output-extraction convention must be applied in three places, and a fix applied to only one silently leaves the other two with divergent failure behavior.
findings.summary: run_model and its FileOutput/list/str extraction logic duplicate ReplicateFluxAdvancedModelBlock.run_model (replicate_flux_advanced.py:186-237) and AIImageGeneratorBlock._run_client (ai_image_generator_block.py:168-196) instead of sharing a helper, creating a third copy to maintain
